description:
Define and implement coherent semantics for the `Archived` lifecycle state and its relationship to dependency-aware artifact archival. Today `Archived` is reachable as a lifecycle state but is not terminal, while container artifact execution requires `Done` or `Rejected`; the intended user workflow and invariant are not yet decided.

## Background

JIT currently has two distinct concepts with overlapping language: an issue can enter lifecycle state `Archived`, and `jit archive container` can relocate linked artifacts. Marking a container `Archived` does not relocate its documents and also makes its artifact plan ineligible because `Archived` is not terminal. Conversely, completing a container and executing artifact archival leaves its lifecycle state as `Done`. This creates a semantic wrinkle for users retiring containers and for descendants whose documents may already have been archived independently.

The resolution may keep the concepts orthogonal, make `Archived` terminal or archive-eligible, introduce an explicit transition sequence, or choose another coherent model. The issue must record the chosen and rejected alternatives with reasons before changing behavior.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Records an explicit decision defining the meaning of lifecycle state `Archived`, whether it is terminal for dependency and readiness semantics, its legal transitions, and its relationship to document/container artifact archival.
- [hard] REQ-02: Applies the chosen semantics consistently across lifecycle transitions, dependency satisfaction, readiness, hierarchy rollups, status and query projections, archive candidates, archive preview, and archive execution.
- [hard] REQ-03: Defines an unambiguous retirement workflow with no circular prerequisite between reaching an eligible lifecycle state and executing artifact archival, including the intended lifecycle state after successful execution.
- [hard] REQ-04: Preserves existing issue records, events, and marker-backed archives safely, with any compatibility behavior or migration requirement explicit and tested rather than inferred from directory names.
- [hard] REQ-05: Emits consistent human and JSON diagnostics that explain the permitted next action whenever lifecycle state makes an artifact archive plan ineligible.
- [hard] REQ-06: Verifies the lifecycle and archive matrix for `Done`, `Rejected`, and `Archived`, including legal and illegal transitions, dependency/readiness effects, parent and descendant archival, independently archived descendants, reruns, and existing repositories.
- [hard] REQ-07: Documents the selected model and user workflow in the canonical lifecycle and archive references without conflating lifecycle state with filesystem relocation.

## Notes

The semantic choice is intentionally open. Alternatives to evaluate include keeping lifecycle and artifact archival orthogonal, treating `Archived` as terminal or archive-eligible, and coupling successful artifact execution to a lifecycle transition. The design must state why the selected model is safer and clearer than the rejected alternatives.

## Decisions pinned by invoker interview (2026-07-16)

- **Archived is terminality-preserving.** Archiving preserves what was true before it: an issue archived from Done/Rejected keeps satisfying dependents; an issue archived from a non-terminal state does not start satisfying them. Rejected: always-terminal (archiving unfinished work would unblock dependents) and never-terminal (retiring finished work would re-block dependents).
- **Coupled retirement workflow.** Artifact archival requires a terminal state (Done/Rejected); successful execution transitions the container to Archived. Rejected: fully orthogonal (manual composition leaves the circular-prerequisite wrinkle) and archived-first eligibility (state change as trigger inverts the safety order).
- **Revive restores the pre-archive state exactly** (done -> archived -> done). A completed issue can never re-enter the active lifecycle via the archive round-trip; this closes the live-verified done -> archived -> ready resurrection loophole. Rejected: free revive + advisory warning (keeps the loophole), no revive (unforgiving of mis-archives).
title: Define Archived lifecycle semantics for artifact archival
